articles.title: Japón mata más de 14.000 osos en diez meses tras dispararse los ataques: el país teme por una especie vulnerable
articles.standfirst: En 2025 se registraron más de 230 ataques de osos, un balance que dejó 13 víctimas mortales, la cifra más alta conocida hasta la fecha
articles.summary: En 2025 se registraron más de 230 ataques de osos, un balance que dejó 13 víctimas mortales, la cifra más alta conocida hasta la fecha
articles.body: Japón se enfrenta a una crisis sin precedentes en la convivencia entre humanos y fauna salvaje. Entre abril de 2025 y enero de 2026, las autoridades del país sacrificaron más de 14.000 osos después de que los encuentros y ataques protagonizados por estos animales aumentaran de forma alarmante en distintas regiones. La cifra refleja la dimensión de un problema que ha ido creciendo en los últimos años. Lo que durante décadas fue considerado un éxito en la conservación de la especie se ha convertido ahora en un problema para las autoridades japonesas, que intentan equilibrar la seguridad de la población con la protección de una fauna cada vez más presente cerca de núcleos urbanos. La situación alcanzó su punto más crítico en 2025. Según los datos oficiales, se registraron más de 230 ataques de osos, un balance que dejó 13 víctimas mortales, la cifra más alta conocida hasta la fecha. Ante el incremento de los incidentes y la escasez de cazadores especializados, el Gobierno japonés optó por flexibilizar las normativas para abatir osos en áreas habitadas. Como consecuencia, más de 14.000 ejemplares fueron eliminados en apenas diez meses. De esa cifra, alrededor de 12.000 correspondieron a osos negros asiáticos y otros 2.000 a osos pardos. Además, las autoridades contemplan eliminar cerca de 8.800 ejemplares adicionales durante el actual ejercicio fiscal para contener el problema. Uno de los casos más representativos se encuentra en Karuizawa, una popular localidad turística rodeada de bosques y montañas. Durante los meses de verano, los osos se acercan con frecuencia a las zonas habitadas en busca de alimento, atraídos por recursos naturales como moras, flores o insectos. Esta situación coincide con la llegada de miles de visitantes, aumentando el riesgo de encuentros peligrosos. Para reducir los conflictos, organizaciones como Picchio llevan décadas desarrollando estrategias de control no letal. Entre ellas destaca el uso de perros especialmente entrenados para ahuyentar a los animales y la captura de ejemplares para reubicarlos en áreas forestales alejadas de la población. La falta de datos precisos preocupa especialmente a los científicos. Los osos son animales solitarios, con amplios territorios y difíciles de contabilizar, por lo que los expertos advierten de que eliminar miles de ejemplares sin conocer el tamaño real de la población puede tener consecuencias graves para la conservación de la especie. "Japón es el país que mejor ha conservado esta especie. El problema es que no planificó con suficiente antelación cómo gestionar el éxito de esa conservación", explica el biólogo Dave Garshelis.

articles.title: IIM Bangalore opens Rs 5 lakh national competition for college students: Eligibility, deadline and how to participate
articles.summary: News News: College students across India have a chance to compete for a Rs 5 lakh prize pool as the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore has opened registrat.
articles.body: College students across India have a chance to compete for a Rs 5 lakh prize pool as the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore has opened registrations for the National Student Case Competition 2026.Organised by the Center for Digital Public Goods (CDPG), IIM Bangalore, with support from Perfios – Anumati Account Aggregator, the competition will challenge student teams to develop solutions to real-world problems linked to India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI).The registration and submission deadline is September 7, 2026, at 6 PM IST.What is the IIM Bangalore National Student Case Competition?The National Student Case Competition 2026 is designed to give students an opportunity to work on practical challenges involving India’s rapidly evolving digital public infrastructure.Participants will work in teams to analyse the announced case or problem and develop an innovative solution. Teams that make it through the initial round will get an opportunity to present their ideas at IIM Bangalore in Bengaluru before practitioners, policymakers and academics.The competition is being organised by CDPG, an initiative at IIM Bangalore focused on research, knowledge creation and policy support around digital public infrastructure and digital public goods.Who can participate?The competition is open to students enrolled in recognised colleges and universities across India.The eligibility requirements include:• Students pursuing Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees can participate.• Students from all academic disciplines are eligible.• Both full-time and part-time students can participate.• Each team must have exactly five students.• Each participant can be part of only one team.• There is no restriction on the number of teams that can participate from a particular college or university.The organisers are also encouraging interdisciplinary teams, bringing together students from areas such as engineering, management, public policy, law, economics, design and social sciences.Why the competition could interest studentsUnlike competitions based purely on academic quizzes or theoretical tests, this case competition asks students to work on issues connected to the country's digital infrastructure.For students, that means an opportunity to apply classroom knowledge to a real-world policy and technology problem.An interdisciplinary team could, for example, bring together different perspectives from technology, business, economics, law and public policy while developing its proposed solution.The organisers are also encouraging teams to be gender-balanced and, where possible, include students from different years and programmes.Rs 5 lakh prize pool and other benefitsThe competition carries a total prize pool of Rs 5 lakh.Beyond the monetary awards, participants can receive certificates of participation and merit. Shortlisted teams will get an opportunity to present their solutions at IIM Bangalore before an audience that includes practitioners, policymakers and academics.Finalists will also have the opportunity to interact with experts attending the CDPG Annual Conclave.For students interested in technology, public policy, management, economics or India's digital transformation, the exposure could be as valuable as the competition itself.Important datesStudents planning to participate should keep the following dates in mind:• Registrations and submissions opened: August 14, 2026• Last date to submit: September 7, 2026, 6 PM IST• Shortlisted teams announced: By September 15, 2026• National Finals: September 30, 2026• Final venue: IIM Bangalore, BengaluruHow the competition will workThe first stage involves submitting a solution to the announced case or theme.After the submissions are evaluated, shortlisted teams will advance to the National Finals. The final round will be held offline at IIM Bangalore, where selected teams will present their ideas to experts from the fields of technology, policy and academia.The requirement of exactly five members means students should form their teams before submitting their entry.What is Digital Public Infrastructure?Digital Public Infrastructure, or DPI, refers broadly to shared digital systems and platforms that can enable large-scale delivery of services, transactions and other public or private-sector applications.India has developed several large-scale digital infrastructure initiatives, making DPI an increasingly important area for technology, governance and public policy discussions.The CDPG at IIM Bangalore focuses on researching such systems, building repositories of data and knowledge, developing case studies and supporting policy and implementation efforts around digital public infrastructure and digital public goods.Why this is an opportunity beyond a college competitionFor students, the National Student Case Competition offers an opportunity to move from simply studying concepts to applying them to a national-scale challenge.The competition also reflects the growing overlap between technology, public policy, business and social impact.With a Rs 5 lakh prize pool, the chance to present at IIM Bangalore and exposure to practitioners and policymakers, the competition could be particularly relevant for students considering careers in technology, consulting, management, public policy, economics or entrepreneurship.Students interested in participating should complete their team formation and submit their entry before September 7, 2026, at 6 PM IST.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. articles.summary: Samantha Adams allegedly slipped benzodiazepines into a drink she gave the 69-year-old victim she met on a dating app, Polk County sheriff says.
articles.body: A Florida woman is behind bars and facing an attempted murder charge after she allegedly drugged a man she’d met on a dating app. Samantha Adams, 39, and the victim, 69, had been in a relationship "for the purposes of…paid sex" for two to three months after meeting online, said Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd.
